title.zh: 卷370 列傳一百五十七 琦善 伊里布 宗室耆英
title.en: Volume 370 Biographies 157: Qi Shan, Yi Libu, Zong Shiqiying
title.raw: 卷370 列傳一百五十七 琦善 伊里布 宗室耆英

sentences.zh: 琦善 琦善，字靜庵，博爾濟吉特氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Qi Shan. Qi Shan, courtesy name Jing'an, of the Borjigit clan, a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan. Qi Shan, whose courtesy name was Jing'an, belonged to the Borjigit clan and came from the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 父成德，熱河都統，以先世格得理爾率屬歸附，世襲一等侯爵。

translations.literal: His father was Chengde, military governor of Rehe; because an ancestor Gedeli'er led his followers to submit, the family inherited a first-class marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengde served as military governor of Rehe. An ancestor named Gedeli'er had led their followers in submission to the dynasty, and the family held an hereditary first-class marquisate.

sentences.zh: 琦善由廕生授刑部員外郎，累遷通政司副使。

translations.literal: Qi Shan entered office through yinsheng privilege as an assistant director in the Ministry of Justice, and was promoted in stages to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan began his career through the yinsheng privilege as an assistant director in the Ministry of Justice and rose step by step to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年，出為河南按察使，歷江寧、河南布政使。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Jiaqing he went out as Henan provincial judicial commissioner, and served successively as provincial treasurer of Jiangning and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 19 he was appointed Henan provincial judicial commissioner and later served as provincial treasurer in Jiangning and Henan.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，擢河南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted to governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of the reign he was promoted to governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 河決馬營壩，偕尚書吳璥督工，甫塞而儀封南岸又決，奪職，予主事銜留工。

translations.literal: The river breached at Ma Ying Dam; together with Minister Wu Jing he supervised the works, but just as the breach was closed the south bank at Yifeng broke again; he was stripped of office and given the rank of secretary while kept on the project.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River burst at Ma Ying Dam, he worked with Minister Wu Jing to supervise repairs. The breach had barely been closed when the south bank at Yifeng gave way again. He lost his post but was given a secretary's rank and kept on the works.

sentences.zh: 尋授河南按察使，調山東。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Henan provincial judicial commissioner and transferred to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Henan provincial judicial commissioner and then transferred to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，就擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was promoted on the spot to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1 he was promoted in place to provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 父憂，奪情任事，襲侯爵。

translations.literal: When his father died he was granted dispensation from mourning to remain in office and inherited the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his father he was allowed to stay in office rather than retire, and he succeeded to the family marquisate.

sentences.zh: 捕治臨清教匪馬進忠，又籌濟高家堰工費八十萬。

translations.literal: He captured and punished the Linqing religious rebel Ma Jinzhong, and also raised eight hundred thousand taels for work on the Gaojia Weir.
translations.idiomatic: He captured and punished the Linqing religious rebel Ma Jinzhong and raised eight hundred thousand taels for repairs to the Gaojia Weir.

sentences.zh: 五年，京察，詔嘉其明幹有為，能任勞怨，加總督銜。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, at the capital inspection, an edict praised his clarity, capability, and willingness to bear hardship and blame, and added the rank of governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the reign, the capital inspection brought an edict praising his clear judgment, effective action, and willingness to bear hardship and blame, and he was given governor-general rank.

sentences.zh: 尋擢兩江總督，兼署漕運總督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to governor-general of Liangjiang and also served concurrently as grain transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to governor-general of Liangjiang and concurrently served as grain transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時高堰屢決，淤運阻漕。

translations.literal: At the time the Gaoji Weir broke repeatedly, silt blocked transport, and grain tribute was obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoji Weir was breaching repeatedly, silt was choking the channel, and grain transport was at a standstill.

sentences.zh: 琦善請用盤運法，並暫行海運，如議行。

translations.literal: Qi Shan requested the use of cart transport and temporary sea transport as well; the proposals were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan proposed cart transport and a temporary shift to sea transport, and both measures were adopted.

sentences.zh: 七年，議啟王家營舊減壩，大濬正河，尋以減壩堵合，黃水倒漾，复閉禦黃壩，漕船倒塘灌放，詔斥失機，議革職，寬之，降授內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year it was proposed to reopen the old relief dam at Wangjiaying and dredge the main channel deeply; soon afterward the relief dam was closed again, Yellow River water backed up, the Yellow River blocking dam was shut once more, and tribute barges were irrigated by reverse channel flow; an edict rebuked him for missing the opportunity, dismissal was proposed, but he was spared and demoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he proposed reopening the old relief dam at Wangjiaying and dredging the main channel. The relief dam was soon closed again, Yellow River water backed up, the blocking dam was shut, and tribute barges had to be filled by reverse irrigation. The court rebuked him for missing his chance, considered dismissing him, but showed leniency and demoted him to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 尋复授山東巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was again appointed governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢四川總督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十一年，調直隸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 十六年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he became associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 十八年，拜文淵閣大學士，仍留總督任。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Deepness and remained in his governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Deepness while retaining his post as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 琦善久膺疆寄，為宣宗所倚任。

translations.literal: Qi Shan had long held frontier responsibilities and was relied upon by Emperor Daoguang.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan had long held important frontier posts and enjoyed the deep trust of Emperor Daoguang.

sentences.zh: 二十年，海疆事急，駐天津籌辦防務。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, with the maritime crisis urgent, he was stationed at Tianjin to organize coastal defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, as the coastal crisis intensified, he was posted to Tianjin to organize the defenses.

sentences.zh: 八月，英兵船至海口，投書乞通商，訴林則徐、鄧廷楨等燒煙啟釁。

translations.literal: In the eighth month British warships reached Haikou, delivered a letter requesting trade, and complained that Lin Zexu, Deng Tingzhen, and others had burned opium and provoked hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month British warships reached Haikou with a letter requesting trade and accusing Lin Zexu, Deng Tingzhen, and others of provoking war by burning opium.

sentences.zh: 琦善招宴英領事義律及兵官，許以代奏。

translations.literal: Qi Shan invited the British consul Elliot and military officers to a banquet and promised to memorialize on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan entertained the British consul Charles Elliot and his officers and promised to submit their petition to the throne.

sentences.zh: 遂入覲面陳，授欽差大臣，赴廣東查辦。

translations.literal: He then entered audience and stated the case in person, was appointed imperial commissioner, and sent to Guangdong to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: He then had an audience with the emperor, was appointed imperial commissioner, and sent to Guangdong to investigate.

sentences.zh: 諭沿海疆吏但防要隘，遇英船毋開砲，義律乃率船回粵。

translations.literal: Coastal officials were instructed only to guard key points and not to open fire on British ships; Elliot then led his fleet back to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal officials were ordered to hold only the key passes and not to fire on British ships, whereupon Elliot led his fleet back to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 尋罷則徐、廷楨，命琦善署兩廣總督兼粵海關監督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Lin Zexu and Deng Tingzhen were dismissed, and Qi Shan was ordered to serve concurrently as governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi and superintendent of Guangdong customs.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu and Deng Tingzhen were soon dismissed, and Qi Shan was ordered to serve as acting governor-general of the two Guang provinces and superintendent of Guangdong customs.

sentences.zh: 密疏臚陳粵事，略曰：「林則徐示令繳煙，許以賞犒，洋人頗存奢望。

translations.literal: In a secret memorial he set out the Guangdong situation in detail, saying in summary: 'Lin Zexu publicly ordered surrender of opium and promised rewards; the foreigners cherished high hopes.
translations.idiomatic: In a secret memorial he laid out the Guangdong situation at length, writing in summary: 'Lin Zexu publicly ordered the surrender of opium and promised rewards and compensation, and the foreigners came to expect much.

sentences.zh: 迨後每煙一箱，僅給茶葉五斤，所得不及本銀百分之一；

translations.literal: Afterward for each chest of opium only five jin of tea was given; what they received did not reach one percent of the original silver value;
translations.idiomatic: Later they received only five jin of tea for each chest of opium—less than one percent of its silver value;

sentences.zh: 又勒具'再販船貨入官、人即正法'甘結，迄未遵依，此釁所由起也。

translations.literal: They were also forced to submit a written pledge that re-smugglers' ships and goods would be confiscated and the persons executed immediately; this was never obeyed, and from this the quarrel arose.
translations.idiomatic: they were also forced to sign a pledge that anyone who smuggled again would forfeit ship and cargo to the state and be executed on the spot, and since this was never accepted, the conflict began here.

sentences.zh: 當義律具禀繳煙，距撤退買辦五日，非出情原。

translations.literal: When Elliot formally petitioned to surrender opium, it was only five days after the compradors were withdrawn; this did not come from genuine goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: When Elliot formally offered to surrender the opium, it was only five days after the compradors had been withdrawn—not a gesture of genuine goodwill.

sentences.zh: 時義律僅止孤身，設有黨援，未必降心俯首。

translations.literal: At the time Elliot was entirely alone; had he had party support, he might not have bowed his head in submission.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Elliot stood entirely alone; had he had allies at his back, he might never have submitted so meekly.

sentences.zh: 英吉利國王無給林則徐文書之事，惟呂宋國王曾有來文，或因此誤傳。

translations.literal: The king of England had sent no letter to Lin Zexu; only the king of Luzon had once sent a communication, and perhaps for this reason the report was mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: The king of England had sent no letter to Lin Zexu; only the king of Luzon had once written, and the story may have arisen from that confusion.

sentences.zh: 林則徐稱定海陰濕，洋人病死甚多。

translations.literal: Lin Zexu claimed that Dinghai was damp and gloomy and that many foreigners had died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu reported that Dinghai was damp and unhealthy and that many foreigners had died of disease there.

sentences.zh: 諮查洋人米穀牲畜尚充，疫癘病斃者多水手舵工，頭目死者不過數人。

translations.literal: On inquiry it was found that the foreigners still had ample grain, rice, and livestock; most who died of epidemic were sailors and helmsmen, and among the officers only a few had died.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiries showed that the foreigners still had ample provisions and livestock; most epidemic deaths were among sailors and helmsmen, and only a few officers had died.

sentences.zh: 從前外洋來信，祗言貿易。

translations.literal: Former letters from overseas spoke only of trade.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier letters from abroad had spoken only of trade.

sentences.zh: 自林則徐欲悉外情，多方購求漁利之人，造作播傳，真偽互見，此時紛紛查探，適墮術中。

translations.literal: Since Lin Zexu wished to know all foreign conditions, he sought out profiteers on every side to fabricate and spread reports, true and false mingled; at this time investigations were launched in all directions and fell straight into the trap.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lin Zexu set out to learn everything about foreign affairs, he paid all sorts of opportunists to manufacture and spread intelligence, mixing truth with falsehood. The frantic inquiries of the moment played straight into their hands.

sentences.zh: 林則徐奏各國憤英人阻其貿易，美利堅、法蘭西將遣船來與理論。

translations.literal: Lin Zexu memorialized that various countries resented the English for blocking their trade and that the United States and France would send ships to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu reported that other nations resented Britain for blocking their trade and that the United States and France would send warships to protest.

sentences.zh: 訪聞各國曾有此說，然迄未見兵船來粵。

translations.literal: On inquiry it was heard that the various countries had indeed said this, yet no warships had yet come to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiries confirmed that such talk had circulated, yet no foreign warships had appeared at Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 前有美國二船，乘英人不備，進口，至今未敢駛出。

translations.literal: Previously two American ships, taking advantage of British inattention, entered port and to this day have not dared to sail out.
translations.idiomatic: Two American ships had slipped into port while the British were off guard and still dared not sail out.

sentences.zh: 畏葸如斯，縱力足頡頏，恐未肯傷其同類。

translations.literal: Timid to such a degree, even if their strength were equal, they would probably not be willing to harm their own kind.
translations.idiomatic: So timid were they that even if strong enough to stand up to the British, they would hardly strike at their own kind.

sentences.zh: 虎門燒煙時，洋人觀者撰文數千言紀事，事誠有之，語多含譏刺，非心服。

translations.literal: At the time of the Humen opium burning, foreign onlookers wrote accounts of several thousand words; the event indeed occurred, but the language was largely sarcastic and did not show heartfelt submission.
translations.idiomatic: When opium was burned at Humen, foreign onlookers wrote lengthy accounts of the event. The event was real enough, but their language was mostly sarcastic—they were far from convinced.

sentences.zh: 林則徐稱具結之後，查驗他國來船，絕無鴉片。

translations.literal: Lin Zexu claimed that after the written pledges were submitted, inspection of ships from other countries found absolutely no opium.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu claimed that once the pledges were signed, inspections of other nations' ships found no opium at all.

sentences.zh: 如指上年而言，事屬以往，船貨無憑；

translations.literal: If this refers to the previous year, the matter belongs to the past and there is no proof of ships and cargo;
translations.idiomatic: If he meant the previous year, that was already past and there was no way to verify ships or cargo;

sentences.zh: 若指本年而言，來船尚未進口，不能知其有，亦安能信其無？

translations.literal: If it refers to this year, the incoming ships have not yet entered port—how can one know they have it, and how can one believe they do not?
translations.idiomatic: if he meant this year, the ships had not yet entered port—how could one know they carried opium, much less swear they did not?

sentences.zh: 」並言將軍阿精阿請團練水勇，及林則徐請鼓勵員弁，俟事定再議。

translations.literal: ' He also said that General A Jing'a had requested training of river militia, and that Lin Zexu's request to encourage officers should wait until affairs were settled.
translations.idiomatic: ' He also reported that General A Jing'a had asked to organize river militia, and that Lin Zexu's proposal to reward officers should wait until the crisis was over.

sentences.zh: 疏入，報聞，則徐以是獲罪。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, it was reported to the throne, and Lin Zexu was punished on this account.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, Lin Zexu was punished on its account.

sentences.zh: 時廣東撤水師歸營，猝被敵轟擊，掠去米艇兵丁，巡撫怡良以聞。

translations.literal: At the time Guangdong had withdrawn the naval forces to barracks; they were suddenly bombarded by the enemy, who carried off grain boats and soldiers; Governor Yi Liang reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong had just withdrawn its naval forces to barracks when the enemy suddenly opened fire, seized grain boats, and captured soldiers. Governor Yi Liang reported the attack.

sentences.zh: 琦善又陳：「英人回粵，詞氣傲慢，義律託疾將回國，且兵船日增。

translations.literal: Qi Shan further reported: 'The English returned to Guangdong with arrogant language; Elliot pleaded illness and would return home, and moreover warships were increasing daily.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan reported further: 'The British returned to Guangdong speaking arrogantly. Elliot claimed illness and said he would go home, while warships were arriving daily.

sentences.zh: 」得旨，仍暫停貿易，一面與議，一面籌防。

translations.literal: ' An edict was received ordering trade still suspended for the time being, negotiating on one hand and preparing defenses on the other.
translations.idiomatic: ' The court ordered trade to remain suspended for now while negotiations continued and defenses were strengthened.

sentences.zh: 義律堅持索還煙價，並增廈門、福州通商，嚴旨拒不許。

translations.literal: Elliot insisted on demanding return of opium compensation and adding Xiamen and Fuzhou for trade; stern orders refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot insisted on compensation for the destroyed opium and on opening Xiamen and Fuzhou to trade, but stern orders from the throne refused both demands.

sentences.zh: 十二月，義律見防禦漸撤，數遣挑戰，琦善諭止之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Elliot saw defenses being gradually withdrawn and repeatedly sent challenges; Qi Shan ordered them stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Elliot saw defenses being drawn down and sent repeated challenges. Qi Shan ordered his men not to respond.

sentences.zh: 義律曰：「戰後再議，未為遲也。

translations.literal: Elliot said: 'After fighting we can negotiate again—it will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot said, 'We can talk again after we fight—it will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 」乃犯虎門外沙角、大角兩砲台，副將陳連升力戰死之，遂陷。

translations.literal: ' He then attacked the two forts at Shajiao and Dajiao outside Humen; vice commander Chen Liansheng fought fiercely and died, and the forts fell.
translations.idiomatic: ' He then attacked the Shajiao and Dajiao forts outside Humen. Vice commander Chen Liansheng fought to the death, and both forts fell.

sentences.zh: 提督關天培守靖遠砲台，總兵李廷鈺守威遠砲台，並請援，琦善不敢明發兵，夜遣二百人往。

translations.literal: Regional commander Guan Tianpei defended Jingyuan Fort and brigade commander Li Tingyu defended Weiyuan Fort; both requested reinforcements, but Qi Shan dared not openly dispatch troops and sent two hundred men by night.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Guan Tianpei held Jingyuan Fort and brigade commander Li Tingyu held Weiyuan Fort. Both asked for help, but Qi Shan dared not send troops openly and sent only two hundred men by night.

sentences.zh: 二十一年正月，事聞，上震怒，下琦善嚴議，命御前大臣貝子奕山為靖逆將軍，戶部尚書隆文、湖南提督楊芳副之，率師赴粵協剿。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-first year, when the matter was reported, the emperor was greatly angered, ordered Qi Shan severely punished, appointed the prince Yishan, an imperial bodyguard grand councilor, as pacification commander, with Minister of Revenue Long Wen and Hunan regional commander Yang Fang as deputies, to lead troops to Guangdong for joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When news reached the court in the first month of the twenty-first year, the emperor was furious. Qi Shan was ordered severely punished. Prince Yishan was named pacification commander, with Minister of Revenue Long Wen and Hunan regional commander Yang Fang as his deputies, and they were sent to Guangdong with an army.

sentences.zh: 義律數索香港，志在必得，琦善當事急，佯許之而不敢上聞。

translations.literal: Elliot repeatedly demanded Hong Kong, determined to obtain it; Qi Shan, with affairs urgent, falsely promised but did not dare report upward.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot repeatedly demanded Hong Kong and meant to have it. With the crisis pressing, Qi Shan pretended to agree but did not dare tell the throne.

sentences.zh: 至是，義律獻出所踞砲台，並原繳還定海以易香港全島，別議通商章程。

translations.literal: At this point Elliot surrendered the forts he held and originally offered to return Dinghai in exchange for the whole island of Hong Kong, with trade regulations to be discussed separately.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot now offered to give up the forts he held and originally proposed returning Dinghai in exchange for the whole of Hong Kong, with trade terms to be negotiated separately.

sentences.zh: 琦善親與相見蓮花城定議，往返傳語，由差遣之鮑鵬將事，同城將軍、巡撫皆不預知。

translations.literal: Qi Shan personally met him at Lotus City to settle terms, passing messages back and forth through the envoy Bao Peng; the garrison general and governor in the same city were not informed beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan met Elliot personally at Lotus City to settle terms, messages passing back and forth through the envoy Bao Peng. The garrison general and provincial governor in the same city knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 及英人佔踞香港，出示安民，巡撫怡良奏聞，琦善方疏陳：「地勢無可扼，軍械無可恃，兵力不固，民情不堅，如與交鋒，實無把握，不如暫事羈縻。

translations.literal: When the English occupied Hong Kong and issued proclamations to reassure the people, Governor Yi Liang memorialized; only then did Qi Shan report: 'The terrain offers no point of control, arms cannot be relied upon, military strength is not solid, and popular sentiment is not firm; if we clashed, there would truly be no certainty—better temporarily to appease.
translations.idiomatic: When the British occupied Hong Kong and issued proclamations to calm the populace, Governor Yi Liang reported it to the throne. Only then did Qi Shan explain: 'The terrain cannot be held, our arms are unreliable, our troops are weak, and the people are unsettled. We have no real chance in a fight—it is better to appease them for now.

sentences.zh: 」上益怒，詔斥琦善擅予香港，擅許通商之罪，褫職逮治，籍沒家產。

translations.literal: ' The emperor grew still angrier and issued an edict rebuking Qi Shan for unauthorized cession of Hong Kong and unauthorized permission to trade; he was stripped of office, arrested, and his property confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor's anger only grew. An edict condemned Qi Shan for ceding Hong Kong and allowing trade without authorization, stripped him of office, ordered his arrest, and confiscated his property.

sentences.zh: 英兵遂奪虎門靖遠砲台，提督關天培死之。

translations.literal: The British troops then seized Jingyuan Fort at Humen, and regional commander Guan Tianpei died.
translations.idiomatic: British forces then took Jingyuan Fort at Humen, and regional commander Guan Tianpei was killed.

sentences.zh: 奕山等至，戰復不利，廣州危急，許以煙價六百萬兩，圍始解，而福建、浙江復被擾。

translations.literal: When Yishan and the others arrived, fighting again went badly; Guangzhou was in peril; six million taels in opium compensation were promised before the siege was lifted, but Fujian and Zhejiang were again disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yishan and his forces arrived, the fighting went badly again. Guangzhou was in grave danger. Six million taels in opium compensation secured a lifting of the siege, but Fujian and Zhejiang were raided anew.

sentences.zh: 琦善逮京，讞論大辟，尋釋之，命赴浙江軍營效力，未至，改發軍台。

translations.literal: Qi Shan was brought to the capital, and judgment called for execution; soon he was released and ordered to serve in the Zhejiang army camp; before he arrived, he was instead sent to a military penal station.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan was brought to the capital and sentenced to death. He was soon released and ordered to serve in the Zhejiang army, but before he arrived he was sent instead to a military penal station.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，浙師复敗，吳淞不守，英兵遂入江，江寧戒嚴，於是耆英、伊里布等定和議，海內莫不以罷戰言和歸咎於琦善為作俑之始矣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the Zhejiang army was defeated again, Wusong could not be held, British troops entered the Yangzi, Jiangning was placed under martial alert, and then Qiying, Yi Libu, and others settled the peace; throughout the realm ending the war and speaking of peace were blamed on Qi Shan as the one who started it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year the Zhejiang forces were beaten again, Wusong fell, British troops entered the Yangzi, and Jiangning went on alert. Qiying, Yi Libu, and others then negotiated peace, and across the empire the decision to stop fighting and sue for peace was blamed on Qi Shan as the man who had set it all in motion.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，予四等侍衛，充葉爾羌幫辦大臣。

translations.literal: That autumn he was given the rank of fourth-class imperial bodyguard and appointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was given fourth-class imperial bodyguard rank and appointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以三品頂戴授熱河都統。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, with third-rank insignia he was appointed military governor of Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was appointed military governor of Rehe with third-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 御史陳慶鏞疏論僨事諸臣罪狀，上重違清議，再褫琦善職，意仍鄉用，未幾，予三等侍衛，充駐藏大臣。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Qingyong memorialized on the offenses of the ministers who had failed in the crisis; the emperor, heavily violating clear opinion, again stripped Qi Shan of office, though still intending eventual reuse; before long he was given third-class bodyguard rank and appointed resident commissioner in Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Qingyong memorialized listing the faults of the ministers who had bungled the crisis. The emperor, going sharply against public opinion, stripped Qi Shan of office again, though still intending to use him later. Before long Qi Shan was given third-class bodyguard rank and appointed resident commissioner in Tibet.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授四川總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，詔嘉其治蜀於吏治營伍實心整頓，复頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year an edict praised his earnest reform of administration and troops in governing Shu, and restored his first-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year an edict praised his earnest reform of civil administration and the army in Sichuan and restored his first-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 尋協辦大學士，留總督任。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he became associate grand secretary while remaining in the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became associate grand secretary while keeping his post as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 以平瞻對野番功被議敘。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying the wild tribes of Zhandui he was recommended for reward.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended for honors for pacifying the tribal peoples of Zhandui.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，調陝甘總督，兼署青海辦事大臣，剿雍沙番及黑城撒拉回匪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu, concurrently serving as Qinghai commissioner, and suppressed the Yusha tribes and Heicheng Salar rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu and concurrently served as Qinghai commissioner, campaigning against the Yusha tribes and the Heicheng Salar rebels.

sentences.zh: 既而言官劾其妄殺，命都統薩迎阿往按，革職逮問。

translations.literal: Afterward censors impeached him for reckless killing; the banner general Saying'a was ordered to investigate; he was dismissed and arrested for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Censors then impeached him for indiscriminate killing. Banner general Saying'a was sent to investigate, and Qi Shan was dismissed and arrested.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，定讞發吉林效力贖罪，尋釋回。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng judgment was fixed to send him to Jilin to redeem his guilt through service; soon he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 2 he was sentenced to serve in Jilin to atone for his crimes and was soon released.

sentences.zh: 時粵匪已犯湖南，勢日熾，屢易帥皆不能制。

translations.literal: At the time the southern rebels had already invaded Hunan; their power grew daily; commanders were changed repeatedly yet none could control them.
translations.idiomatic: Southern rebels had already invaded Hunan, their strength growing daily. Commanders were changed again and again, yet none could check them.

sentences.zh: 起琦善署河南巡撫，駐防楚、豫界上。

translations.literal: Qi Shan was recalled to serve as acting governor of Henan, stationed on the border of Huguang and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan was recalled to serve as acting governor of Henan, posted on the border between Huguang and Henan.

sentences.zh: 以捐餉加都統銜，授欽差大臣，專辦防務。

translations.literal: For donating military funds he was given banner general rank and appointed imperial commissioner in charge of defenses alone.
translations.idiomatic: For contributing military funds he was given banner general rank and appointed imperial commissioner with sole charge of the defenses.

sentences.zh: 湖北省城失守，觀望不能救。

translations.literal: The provincial capital of Hubei fell; he looked on and could not save it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hubei provincial capital fell, he held back and could not relieve it.

sentences.zh: 三年春，賊遂連陷安徽、江寧省城，分擾鎮江、揚州，命琦善偕直隸提督陳金​​綬防江北。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year the rebels then captured in succession the provincial capitals of Anhui and Jiangning, and sent detachments to harass Zhenjiang and Yangzhou; Qi Shan was ordered together with Zhili regional commander Chen Jinshou to defend the north bank of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year the rebels took the capitals of Anhui and Jiangning in succession and raided Zhenjiang and Yangzhou. Qi Shan was ordered to join Zhili regional commander Chen Jinshou in defending the north bank of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 三月，連敗賊於浦口雷塘，進剿揚州，分屯寶塔山、司徒廟，五戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In the third month he repeatedly defeated the rebels at Pukou and Leitang, advanced to suppress Yangzhou, and encamped separately at Baota Hill and Situgong Temple; five battles were all victories.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he beat the rebels repeatedly at Pukou and Leitang, advanced against Yangzhou, and encamped at Baota Hill and Situgong Temple, winning five engagements in a row.

sentences.zh: 秋，破浦口援賊，合圍揚州。

translations.literal: In autumn he broke the rebel reinforcements at Pukou and jointly besieged Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn he routed rebel reinforcements at Pukou and closed the ring around Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，賊突圍出竄瓜洲，以收復揚州入告，詔斥勇潰縱賊，責令進剿瓜洲、儀徵，儀徵克復。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the rebels broke out and fled to Guazhou; he reported the recovery of Yangzhou; an edict rebuked the troops for breaking and letting the rebels escape, ordered pursuit of Guazhou and Yizheng, and Yizheng was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the rebels broke out and fled to Guazhou. Qi Shan reported the recovery of Yangzhou, but an edict rebuked his troops for letting the enemy escape and ordered him to pursue them at Guazhou and Yizheng. Yizheng was retaken.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，連戰金川、瓜洲、三汊河，屢奏斬獲。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year he fought continuously at Jinchuan, Guazhou, and San Chahe, repeatedly reporting beheadings and captures.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year he fought repeatedly at Jinchuan, Guazhou, and San Chahe and reported many kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 自琦善與向榮分主大江南北軍事，攻戰年餘，鎮江、瓜洲迄未克復，無得力水師，不能扼賊，琦善雖議增水師，亦未果。

translations.literal: From the time Qi Shan and Xiang Rong divided command of military affairs north and south of the Yangzi, fighting went on for more than a year; Zhenjiang and Guazhou were still not recovered; without effective naval forces they could not choke the rebels; although Qi Shan proposed increasing the navy, this too did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qi Shan and Xiang Rong divided command of the armies north and south of the Yangzi, fighting dragged on for more than a year. Zhenjiang and Guazhou remained untaken. Without a capable navy they could not block the rebels, and though Qi Shan proposed building one up, that too came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，卒於軍，贈太子太保、協辦大學士，依總督例賜卹，諡文勤。

translations.literal: That autumn he died in camp; he was posthumously given Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and associate grand secretary, granted mourning benefits according to the governor-general precedent, and given the posthumous name Wenqin.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he died in camp. He was posthumously made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and associate grand secretary, granted mourning honors befitting a governor-general, and given the posthumous name Wenqin.

sentences.zh: 恭鏜 子恭鏜，黑龍江將軍。

translations.literal: Gongtang. His son Gongtang was general of Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gongtang. His son Gongtang served as general of Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 孫瑞洵，烏里雅蘇台參贊大臣；

translations.literal: His grandson Ruixun was commissioner at Uliastai;
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Ruixun served as commissioner at Uliastai;

sentences.zh: 瑞澂，兩湖總督。

translations.literal: Ruicheng was governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Ruicheng served as governor-general of the two Hu provinces.

sentences.zh: 瑞澂自有傳。

translations.literal: Ruicheng has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Ruicheng has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 伊里布 伊里布，字莘農，鑲黃旗紅帶子。

translations.literal: Yi Libu. Yi Libu, courtesy name Xinnong, a 'red girdle' descendant of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Libu. Yi Libu, whose courtesy name was Xinnong, was a 'red girdle' descendant of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年進士，授國子監學正，改補典簿。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the sixth year of Jiaqing, he was appointed director of studies at the Imperial Academy and later transferred to clerical officer.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Jiaqing 6, was appointed director of studies at the Imperial Academy, and later transferred to a clerical post.

sentences.zh: 出為雲南府南關通判，署澂江知府，遷騰越知州。

translations.literal: He went out as sub-prefect at Yunnan's southern gate, acted as prefect of Chengjiang, and was transferred to magistrate of Tengyue.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as sub-prefect at Yunnan's southern gate, served as acting prefect of Chengjiang, and was promoted to magistrate of Tengyue.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，總督伯麟薦其熟練邊務，能馭土司，治緬匪有功，以應升用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Governor-General Bo Lin recommended him as skilled in frontier affairs, able to control native chiefs, and meritorious in handling Burmese rebels, for promotion as due.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year Governor-General Bo Lin recommended him as experienced in frontier affairs, skilled at managing native chiefs, and successful against Burmese rebels, and he was promoted accordingly.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，從總督慶保剿平永北大姚夷匪，賜花翎，署永昌知府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang, following Governor-General Qingbao he suppressed the Yongbei Dayao tribal rebels, was granted the peacock feather, and acted as prefect of Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1 he followed Governor-General Qingbao in suppressing the Yongbei Dayao tribal rebels, was awarded the peacock feather, and served as acting prefect of Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 擢安徽太平知府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Taiping in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Taiping in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 歷山西冀寧道，浙江按察使，湖北、浙江布政使。

translations.literal: He served successively as Jining circuit intendant in Shanxi, Zhejiang provincial judicial commissioner, and provincial treasurer of Hubei and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Jining circuit intendant in Shanxi, Zhejiang provincial judicial commissioner, and provincial treasurer in Hubei and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢陝西巡撫，調山東。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to governor of Shaanxi and transferred to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to governor of Shaanxi and then transferred to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，署雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: During mourning for his father he acted as governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his father he served as acting governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 服闋，乃實授。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he received formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he received the appointment in full.

sentences.zh: 時阮元為總督，伊里布和而廉，有政聲。

translations.literal: At the time Ruan Yuan was governor-general; Yi Libu was conciliatory and incorrupt, and had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: While Ruan Yuan served as governor-general, Yi Libu was known as conciliatory and upright, and enjoyed a reputation for sound administration.

sentences.zh: 回疆兵事起，自請從軍，詔斥不諳回情，妄行陳奏，奪職留任，尋復之。

translations.literal: When military affairs arose in the Muslim frontier, he volunteered to join the campaign; an edict rebuked him for not understanding Muslim conditions and rashly memorializing, stripped him of rank but kept him in office, and soon restored it.
translations.idiomatic: When fighting broke out on the Muslim frontier, he volunteered for the campaign. An edict rebuked him for not understanding frontier conditions and for rash memorializing, stripped him of rank while keeping him in post, and soon restored it.

sentences.zh: 十三年，擢雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 京察，以久任邊疆，鎮撫得宜，被議敘。

translations.literal: At the capital inspection, for long service on the frontier and proper pacification he was recommended for reward.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital inspection he was recommended for honors for his long service on the frontier and effective pacification.

sentences.zh: 十八年，協辦大學士，留總督任。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he became associate grand secretary while remaining in the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was made associate grand secretary while keeping his post as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 四川綦江奸民穆繼賢仇殺貴州仁懷武生趙應彩，遂糾眾踞方家溝為亂，伊里布率提督余步雲、布政使慶祿等破其巢，斬獲千餘，誅賊首穆繼賢、謝法真等，餘匪悉平，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: The rogue of Qijiang in Sichuan, Mu Jixian, killed in feud the military licentiate Zhao Yingcai of Renhuai in Guizhou, then gathered a mob and seized Fangjiagou in rebellion; Yi Libu led regional commander Yu Buyun, provincial treasurer Qing Lu, and others to destroy their lair, beheading and capturing more than a thousand, executed the rebel leaders Mu Jixian, Xie Fazhen, and others, pacified the remaining bandits entirely, and was granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Jixian, a rogue of Qijiang in Sichuan, killed Zhao Yingcai, a military licentiate of Renhuai in Guizhou, in a feud, then rallied a mob and seized Fangjiagou in revolt. Yi Libu led regional commander Yu Buyun, provincial treasurer Qing Lu, and others to destroy their stronghold, killing and capturing more than a thousand. The rebel leaders Mu Jixian and Xie Fazhen were executed and the rest of the bandits were pacified. He was awarded the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 十九年，調兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to governor-general of Liangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to governor-general of Liangjiang.

sentences.zh: 二十年秋，英兵陷定海，命為欽差大臣，赴浙江查辦。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twentieth year, when British troops took Dinghai, he was appointed imperial commissioner and sent to Zhejiang to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the twentieth year, after British troops took Dinghai, he was appointed imperial commissioner and sent to Zhejiang to investigate.

sentences.zh: 時已有論致寇由斷絕貿易燒煙起釁者，密諭察訪確情毋回護。

translations.literal: At the time there were already arguments that the enemy had been provoked by cutting off trade and burning opium; a secret instruction ordered investigation of the true facts without cover-up.
translations.idiomatic: Some already argued that the enemy had been provoked by cutting off trade and burning opium. A secret instruction ordered him to investigate the facts without shielding anyone.

sentences.zh: 尋以琦善代林則徐，命沿海遇敵勿擊。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Qi Shan replaced Lin Zexu, and coastal officials were ordered not to attack when they met the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan soon replaced Lin Zexu, and coastal officials were ordered not to engage the enemy.

sentences.zh: 伊里布初至浙，駐鎮海籌防，疏報擊沉敵船，有所擒獲，命慰諭英人攻擊出於誤會，促令退兵交地，俘虜俟敵退釋還。

translations.literal: When Yi Libu first reached Zhejiang he was stationed at Zhenhai organizing defenses; he memorialized that enemy ships had been sunk and captives taken; he was ordered to reassure the English that the attack arose from misunderstanding, urge them to withdraw and return territory, and release prisoners after the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi Libu first reached Zhejiang he was posted at Zhenhai to organize the defenses. He reported sinking enemy ships and taking captives. The court ordered him to assure the British that the attack was a misunderstanding, urge them to withdraw and return occupied territory, and release prisoners once they did.

sentences.zh: 伊里布遣家丁張喜偕員弁赴定海犒師，英人亦答餽，奏聞，諭卻勿受。

translations.literal: Yi Libu sent his household servant Zhang Xi together with officers to Dinghai to reward the troops; the English also returned gifts; this was reported, and he was instructed to refuse and not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Libu sent his servant Zhang Xi with officers to Dinghai to reward the troops. The British sent gifts in return. When he reported this, the court ordered him to refuse them.

sentences.zh: 請增調安徽、兩湖兵，允之。

translations.literal: He requested additional troops from Anhui and the two Hu provinces; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for reinforcements from Anhui and the two Hu provinces, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 裕謙方代署兩江總督，疏言：「各省皆可議守，獨浙江必應速戰。

translations.literal: Yu Qian was then acting governor-general of Liangjiang and memorialized: 'Every province may discuss defense, but Zhejiang alone must fight quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian, then acting governor-general of Liangjiang, memorialized: 'Every province may talk of holding defensive positions, but Zhejiang must fight at once.

sentences.zh: 」且言：「定海西境岑港為第一險要，應以精兵先據之。

translations.literal: ' He also said: 'Cengang on the western border of Dinghai is the foremost strategic point and should be seized first by elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: ' He added: 'Cengang on Dinghai's western border is the most critical point and should be occupied first by elite troops.

sentences.zh: 」下伊里布體察辦理。

translations.literal: ' The matter was referred to Yi Libu for investigation and handling.
translations.idiomatic: ' The order was sent to Yi Libu to investigate and act accordingly.

sentences.zh: 既而琦善在粵議款不得要領，兵端又開，二十一年正月，詔促伊里布進兵規复定海。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Qi Shan's negotiations in Guangdong failed to reach essentials, and hostilities reopened; in the first month of the twenty-first year an edict urged Yi Libu to advance and recover Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan's negotiations in Guangdong then broke down and fighting resumed. In the first month of the twenty-first year an edict ordered Yi Libu to advance and retake Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 二月，義律既踞香港，盡調英船赴粵，以交還定海告。

translations.literal: In the second month Elliot, having seized Hong Kong, transferred all British ships to Guangdong and announced the return of Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Elliot, having taken Hong Kong, moved all British ships to Guangdong and offered to return Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 詔斥附和琦善，以兵砲未集，藉詞緩攻，致敵船遁去，褫協辦大學士、雙眼花翎，暫留兩江總督任，以裕謙代為欽差大臣督浙師。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked him for siding with Qi Shan, using the excuse that troops and guns were not assembled to delay the attack and letting enemy ships escape; he was stripped of associate grand secretary rank and the double-eyed peacock feather, temporarily kept as governor-general of Liangjiang, and Yu Qian replaced him as imperial commissioner commanding the Zhejiang army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict condemned him for echoing Qi Shan, delaying the attack on the pretext that troops and artillery were not ready, and letting the enemy fleet escape. He lost his associate grand secretary rank and double-eyed peacock feather but kept the Liangjiang governorship for the time being. Yu Qian replaced him as imperial commissioner in command of the Zhejiang forces.

sentences.zh: 裕謙論劾伊里布遣家丁赴敵船事，命解任，帶張喜來京，下刑部訊鞫，褫職，遣戍軍台。

translations.literal: Yu Qian impeached Yi Libu for sending his household servant to the enemy ships; he was ordered relieved of duty, brought Zhang Xi to the capital, handed over to the Ministry of Justice for interrogation, stripped of office, and sent to a military penal station.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian impeached Yi Libu for sending his servant to the enemy ships. He was relieved of duty, Zhang Xi was brought to the capital, and Yi Libu was interrogated by the Ministry of Justice, stripped of office, and exiled to a military penal station.

sentences.zh: 未幾，定海、鎮海、寧波相繼陷，裕謙殉之。

translations.literal: Before long Dinghai, Zhenhai, and Ningbo fell in succession, and Yu Qian died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Dinghai, Zhenhai, and Ningbo fell in succession, and Yu Qian died defending them.

sentences.zh: 二十二年春，揚威將軍奕經援浙，復挫敗。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-second year Pacification General Yijing came to aid Zhejiang and was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-second year Pacification General Yijing marched to relieve Zhejiang and was beaten again.

sentences.zh: 巡撫劉韻珂疏陳浙事危急，薦伊里布無急功近名之心，為一時僅見，請發軍營效力贖罪。

translations.literal: Governor Liu Yunke memorialized that Zhejiang affairs were critical, recommended Yi Libu as free of eagerness for quick success and fame, a rare man of the time, and requested that he be sent to serve in the army to redeem his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Yunke reported that Zhejiang was in grave danger and recommended Yi Libu as a man without hunger for quick glory—a rare quality in those days—and asked that he be sent to serve in the army to atone for his faults.

sentences.zh: 於是予七品頂戴，隨杭州將軍耆英赴浙，密諭相機辦理。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was given seventh-rank insignia, followed Hangzhou General Qiying to Zhejiang, and received secret instructions to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: He was then given seventh-rank insignia, accompanied Hangzhou General Qiying to Zhejiang, and received secret orders to act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 及英兵犯乍浦，耆英遣往設計退兵。

translations.literal: When British troops attacked Zhapu, Qiying sent him to devise a plan to make them withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When British forces attacked Zhapu, Qiying sent him to find a way to make them withdraw.

sentences.zh: 五月，署乍浦副都統，復令張喜傳語，英兵遂去乍浦，犯吳淞，由海入江，鎮江失守。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he acted as vice commander at Zhapu, again had Zhang Xi convey messages, the British troops then left Zhapu, attacked Wusong, entered the Yangzi from the sea, and Zhenjiang fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he served as acting vice commander at Zhapu and again used Zhang Xi as an intermediary. The British left Zhapu, attacked Wusong, entered the Yangzi from the sea, and Zhenjiang fell.

sentences.zh: 伊里布奉命偕耆英赴江寧議和，事詳耆英傳。

translations.literal: Yi Libu was ordered together with Qiying to go to Jiangning to negotiate peace; details are given in Qiying's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Libu was ordered to join Qiying in Jiangning to negotiate peace; the details are given in Qiying's biography.

sentences.zh: 和議既成，英兵退，約於廣東議稅則，命偕耆英詳慎酌商，授廣州將軍、欽差大臣，辦理善後事宜。

translations.literal: Once peace was settled and British troops withdrew, it was agreed to discuss tariff regulations in Guangdong; he was ordered together with Qiying to deliberate carefully, appointed general of Guangzhou and imperial commissioner, and charged with postwar arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made and the British withdrew, tariff terms were to be negotiated in Guangdong. He was ordered to consult carefully with Qiying, appointed general of Guangzhou and imperial commissioner, and put in charge of postwar arrangements.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，至粵，見民心不服，夷情狡橫，憂悴。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he reached Guangdong, saw that popular sentiment was unreconciled and foreign attitudes crafty and overbearing, and was worn with worry.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he reached Guangdong, found the people unreconciled and foreign attitudes crafty and arrogant, and was consumed with worry.

sentences.zh: 踰月病卒，贈太子太保，諡文敏。

translations.literal: After little more than a month he died of illness; he was posthumously given Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later he died of illness. He was posthumously made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 宗室耆英 宗室耆英，字介春，隸正藍旗。

translations.literal: Qiying of the Imperial Clan. Qiying, courtesy name Jiechun, belonged to the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying of the Imperial Clan. Qiying, whose courtesy name was Jiechun, belonged to the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 父祿康，嘉慶間官東閣大學士。

translations.literal: His father was Lukang, who in the Jiaqing reign served as grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lukang had served as grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion under Jiaqing.

sentences.zh: 耆英以廕生授宗人府主事，遷理事官。

translations.literal: Qiying entered through yinsheng privilege as a secretary in the Imperial Clan Court and was transferred to administrative officer.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying entered service through the yinsheng privilege as a secretary in the Imperial Clan Court and was later made an administrative officer.

sentences.zh: 累擢內閣學士，兼副都統、護軍統​​領。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to Grand Secretariat academician, concurrently serving as vice banner general and commandant of the guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Grand Secretariat academician, concurrently serving as vice banner general and commandant of the guard.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，遷理籓院侍郎，調兵部。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he was transferred to vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and then to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 2 he was transferred to vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and then to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 四年，送宗室閒散移駐雙城堡。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he escorted idle members of the imperial clan to relocate to Shuangcheng Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he escorted idle members of the imperial clan to their new settlement at Shuangcheng Fort.

sentences.zh: 五年，授內務府大臣，歷工部、戶部。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed minister of the Imperial Household Department and served successively in the Ministries of Works and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed minister of the Imperial Household Department and later served in the Ministries of Works and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 七年，授步軍統領。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed commandant of the metropolitan gendarmerie.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed commandant of the metropolitan gendarmerie.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢禮部尚書，管理太常寺、鴻​​臚寺、太醫院，兼都統。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to minister of Rites, administered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the Court of State Ceremonial, and the Imperial Medical Academy, and concurrently served as banner general.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to minister of Rites, placed in charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the Court of State Ceremonial, and the Imperial Medical Academy, and concurrently served as banner general.

sentences.zh: 十二年，畿輔旱，疏請察吏省刑，嘉納之，授內大臣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, during drought in the capital region, he memorialized requesting inspection of officials and reduction of punishments; this was praised and accepted, and he was appointed inner court minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, during drought in the capital region, he memorialized asking for tighter oversight of officials and lighter punishments. The emperor approved and made him an inner court minister.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以管理步軍統領勤事，被議敘。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, for diligent service managing the metropolitan gendarmerie, he was recommended for reward.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was recommended for honors for diligent management of the metropolitan gendarmerie.

sentences.zh: 歷工部、戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He served successively as minister of Works and minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as minister of Works and minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以相度龍泉峪萬年吉地，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, for surveying the auspicious burial site at Longquanyu for ten thousand years, he was given Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, for surveying the imperial burial site at Longquanyu, he was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 命赴廣東、江西按事。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go to Guangdong and Jiangxi to investigate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to Guangdong and Jiangxi to investigate local affairs.

sentences.zh: 十七年，內監張道忠犯賭博，耆英瞻徇釋放，事覺，降兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the eunuch Zhang Daozhong was guilty of gambling; Qiying looked on favorably and released him; when the matter came to light he was demoted to vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the eunuch Zhang Daozhong was caught gambling. Qiying looked the other way and released him. When the affair came to light he was demoted to vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 尋出為熱河都統。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he went out as military governor of Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted as military governor of Rehe.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授盛京將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed general of Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was appointed general of Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 詔嚴禁鴉片，無論宗室、覺羅，按律懲治。

translations.literal: An edict strictly forbade opium; whether imperial clansmen or aisin gioro, all were to be punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: An edict strictly forbade opium and ordered that imperial clansmen and aisin gioro alike be punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 疏請旗民十家聯保，以憑稽察。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting mutual guarantee groups of ten banner households for purposes of inspection.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking that banner households be organized in mutual guarantee groups of ten for inspection.

sentences.zh: 二十年，海疆戒嚴，疏請旅順口為水路衝衢，當扼要籌備。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, with the maritime frontier on alert, he memorialized that Lüshunkou was a strategic waterway junction and should be fortified at key points.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, as the coast went on alert, he memorialized that Lüshunkou was a critical waterway junction and should be fortified.

sentences.zh: 英船入奉天洋面，先後游弋山海關、秦皇島等處，錦州、山海關皆設防。

translations.literal: British ships entered the waters off Fengtian and successively cruised off Shanhaiguan, Qinhuangdao, and other places; defenses were set at Jinzhou and Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: British ships entered the waters off Fengtian and cruised off Shanhaiguan, Qinhuangdao, and other points. Defenses were raised at Jinzhou and Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 二十二年正月，粵事急，琦善既黜，調耆英廣州將軍，授欽差大臣，督辦浙江洋務。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-second year, with Guangdong affairs urgent and Qi Shan already dismissed, Qiying was transferred to general of Guangzhou, appointed imperial commissioner, and put in charge of Zhejiang maritime affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-second year, with Guangdong in crisis and Qi Shan already dismissed, Qiying was transferred to general of Guangzhou, made imperial commissioner, and put in charge of Zhejiang maritime affairs.

sentences.zh: 因御史蘇廷魁奏英吉利為鄰國所破，詔促耆英赴廣州本任，乘機進剿，尋知其訛傳，仍留浙江。

translations.literal: Because Censor Su Tingkui memorialized that England had been defeated by neighboring countries, an edict urged Qiying to proceed to his regular post at Guangzhou and seize the chance to advance in suppression; soon it was learned this was false report, and he remained in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Su Tingkui reported that England had been defeated by neighboring powers, the court ordered Qiying to hurry to his post at Guangzhou and strike while the enemy was weak. The story proved false, and he remained in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 五月，吳淞失守，命偕伊里布赴江蘇相機籌辦。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, when Wusong fell, he was ordered together with Yi Libu to go to Jiangsu and handle matters as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, after Wusong fell, he was ordered to join Yi Libu in Jiangsu and handle affairs as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 英兵已入江，越圌山關，陷鎮江，踞瓜洲，耆英與揚威將軍奕經先後奏請羈縻招撫。

translations.literal: British troops had already entered the Yangzi, passed Tuishan Pass, taken Zhenjiang, and occupied Guazhou; Qiying and Pacification General Yijing successively memorialized requesting appeasement and conciliation.
translations.idiomatic: British troops had entered the Yangzi, passed Tuishan Pass, taken Zhenjiang, and occupied Guazhou. Qiying and Pacification General Yijing both memorialized asking to appease and conciliate the enemy.

sentences.zh: 七月，英兵薄江寧下關，伊里布先至，英人索煙價、商欠、戰費共二千一百萬兩，廣州、福州、廈門、寧波、上海五港通商，英官與中國官員用平行禮，及劃抵關稅、釋放漢奸等款。

translations.literal: In the seventh month British troops approached Xiaguan at Jiangning; Yi Libu arrived first; the English demanded opium compensation, merchant debts, and war costs totaling twenty-one million taels, trade at five ports—Guangzhou, Fuzhou, Xiamen, Ningbo, and Shanghai—parallel protocol between English and Chinese officials, and provisions on offsetting customs duties and releasing Chinese collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month British troops approached Xiaguan below Jiangning. Yi Libu arrived first. The British demanded twenty-one million taels for opium compensation, merchant debts, and war costs; trade at Guangzhou, Fuzhou, Xiamen, Ningbo, and Shanghai; equal ceremonial status for British and Chinese officials; and terms on customs offsets and the release of Chinese collaborators.

sentences.zh: 越三日，耆英至，稍稍駁詰之。

translations.literal: Three days later Qiying arrived and mildly raised objections.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Qiying arrived and raised mild objections.

sentences.zh: 英兵突張紅旗，置砲鍾山上臨城，急止之，遣侍衛咸齡、江寧布政使恩彤、寧紹台道鹿澤良，偕伊里布家丁張喜，詣英舟，許據情奏聞。

translations.literal: British troops suddenly raised red flags and placed guns on Zhongshan overlooking the city; he urgently stopped this, sent bodyguard Xianling, Jiangning provincial treasurer Entong, Ning-Shao-Tai circuit intendant Lu Zeliang, together with Yi Libu's servant Zhang Xi, to the British ships, and promised to memorialize according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: British troops suddenly raised red flags and mounted guns on Zhongshan overlooking the city. He urgently stopped them and sent bodyguard Xianling, Jiangning provincial treasurer Entong, Ning-Shao-Tai circuit intendant Lu Zeliang, and Yi Libu's servant Zhang Xi to the British ships, promising to report the terms to the throne.

sentences.zh: 宣宗憤甚，大學士穆彰阿以糜餉勞師無效、剿與撫費亦相等為言，乃允之。

translations.literal: Emperor Daoguang was greatly angered; Grand Secretary Mujangga argued that wasting funds and exhausting troops had been ineffective and that suppression and appeasement cost equally; only then was it approved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daoguang was furious, but Grand Secretary Mujangga argued that the campaign had wasted funds and manpower to no effect and that fighting and appeasing would cost the same. The terms were then approved.

sentences.zh: 耆英等與英將濮鼎查、馬利遜會盟於儀鳳門外靜海寺，同籤條約，先予六百萬，餘分三年給，和議遂成。

translations.literal: Qiying and the others met in alliance with the British generals Pottinger and Morrison at Jinghai Temple outside Yifeng Gate, jointly signed the treaty, gave six million first with the remainder paid over three years, and peace was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying and his party met the British generals Pottinger and Morrison at Jinghai Temple outside Yifeng Gate and signed the treaty. Six million taels were paid at once and the rest over three years, and peace was made.

sentences.zh: 九月，英兵盡數駛出吳淞，授兩江總督，命籌辦通商及浙江、福建因地制宜之策。

translations.literal: In the ninth month all British troops sailed out of Wusong; he was appointed governor-general of Liangjiang and ordered to organize trade and devise policies suited to local conditions in Zhejiang and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month all British troops left Wusong. He was appointed governor-general of Liangjiang and ordered to organize trade and devise policies suited to local conditions in Zhejiang and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，授欽差大臣，赴廣東議通商章程，就粵海關稅則分別增減，各口按新例一體開關，臚列整頓稅務條款，下廷議施行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was appointed imperial commissioner, sent to Guangdong to negotiate trade regulations, adjusted tariffs at Guangdong customs with separate increases and reductions, opened all ports uniformly under the new rules, set out in detail provisions for reorganizing tax affairs, and submitted them to court deliberation for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was made imperial commissioner and sent to Guangdong to negotiate trade regulations. He adjusted Guangdong customs tariffs, opened all ports under the new rules, laid out detailed provisions for tax reform, and submitted them to the court for approval.

sentences.zh: 又奏美利堅、法蘭西等國一體通商，允之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that the United States, France, and other countries should trade on the same terms; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that the United States, France, and other countries should be allowed to trade on the same terms, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 美國請入京瞻覲，卻不許。

translations.literal: The United States requested an audience in the capital; this was refused.
translations.idiomatic: The United States requested an imperial audience in the capital, but the request was refused.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，調授兩廣總督，兼辦通商事宜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred and appointed governor-general of the two Guang provinces, concurrently handling trade affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to governor-general of the two Guang provinces with concurrent charge of trade affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，協辦大學士，留總督任。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he became associate grand secretary while remaining in the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was made associate grand secretary while keeping his post as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 比利時、丹麥等國請通商，命體察約束。

translations.literal: Belgium, Denmark, and other countries requested trade; he was ordered to investigate and impose restrictions.
translations.idiomatic: Belgium, Denmark, and other countries asked to trade, and he was ordered to investigate and set appropriate limits.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，京察，以殫心竭慮坐鎮海疆，被議敘。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, at the capital inspection, for devoting heart and mind to holding the maritime frontier he was recommended for reward.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital inspection in the twenty-sixth year he was recommended for honors for his devoted stewardship of the maritime frontier.

sentences.zh: 疏上練兵事宜，繕呈唐臣陸贄守備事宜狀，請下各將軍督撫置諸座右。

translations.literal: He memorialized on troop training, transcribed and presented Tang minister Lu Zhi's memorial on defense preparedness, and requested that it be sent to all generals and governors to keep at their desks.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on troop training, transcribed Tang minister Lu Zhi's memorial on defense preparedness, and asked that copies be sent to every general and governor to keep at hand.

sentences.zh: 英國請於西藏定界通商，諭耆英堅守成約，毋為搖惑。

translations.literal: Britain requested demarcation and trade in Tibet; Qiying was instructed to hold firmly to existing treaties and not be swayed.
translations.idiomatic: Britain requested boundary demarcation and trade in Tibet. Qiying was instructed to hold to existing treaties and not be swayed.

sentences.zh: 故事，廣東洋商居住澳門，貿易有定界，赴洋行發貨，不得擅入省城。

translations.literal: By precedent foreign merchants in Guangdong lived in Macao, trade had fixed boundaries, and in shipping goods through the foreign factories they were not permitted to enter the provincial capital without authorization.
translations.idiomatic: By long-standing practice foreign merchants in Guangdong lived in Macao, trade was confined to fixed areas, and they were not allowed to enter the provincial capital except through the foreign factories.

sentences.zh: 自江寧和議有省城設立棧房及領事入城之約，粵民猶持舊例，愬於大吏，不省，乃舉團練，眾議洶洶，不受官吏約束。

translations.literal: Since the Jiangning peace treaty provided for warehouses in the provincial capital and consuls entering the city, Guangdong people still held to old precedent and petitioned the high officials without understanding; then they raised militia training, public opinion grew turbulent, and they would not accept official restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangning treaty provided for warehouses in the provincial capital and for consuls to enter the city, but Guangdong people clung to the old rules and petitioned the high officials in vain. They then organized militia training; public opinion grew heated, and they refused official control.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，濮鼎查將入城，粵民不可，逡巡去。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Pottinger was about to enter the city; Guangdong people would not permit it, and he withdrew after hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year Pottinger was about to enter the city, but Guangdong people would not allow it, and he withdrew after hesitating.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，英船復至，耆英遣廣州知府餘保純詣商，粵民鼓譟，安撫乃罷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year British ships came again; Qiying sent Guangzhou prefect Yu Baochun to negotiate with the merchants; Guangdong people clamored loudly, and after pacification the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year British ships returned. Qiying sent Guangzhou prefect Yu Baochun to negotiate with the merchants, but Guangdong people raised an uproar, and the effort was abandoned after pacification.

sentences.zh: 英人以登岸每遭窘辱，貽書大吏誚讓，群情憤激，不可曉諭。

translations.literal: Because the English were humiliated whenever they came ashore, they sent letters to the high officials reproaching them; public sentiment was furious and could not be persuaded.
translations.idiomatic: The British complained in letters to the high officials that their men were humiliated whenever they came ashore. Public anger ran too high to be reasoned with.

sentences.zh: 至二十七年，英船突入省河，要求益堅，耆英謾許兩年後踐約，始退，自請議處。

translations.literal: By the twenty-seventh year British ships suddenly entered the provincial river; their demands grew firmer; Qiying falsely promised fulfillment in two years before they withdrew, and he requested punishment for himself.
translations.idiomatic: By the twenty-seventh year British ships suddenly entered the provincial river with firmer demands. Qiying vaguely promised fulfillment in two years, and they withdrew only then. He asked to be punished.

sentences.zh: 諭嚴為防備，務出萬全。

translations.literal: An instruction ordered strict defense and absolute precaution.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to strengthen the defenses and leave nothing to chance.

sentences.zh: 耆英知終必有釁。

translations.literal: Qiying knew that trouble would come in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying knew trouble was inevitable in the end.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，請入覲，留京供職，賜雙眼花翎，管理禮部、兵部，兼都統。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he requested an audience, remained in the capital to serve, was granted the double-eyed peacock feather, and administered the Ministries of Rites and War while concurrently serving as banner general.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he requested an audience, remained in the capital to serve, was awarded the double-eyed peacock feather, and was placed in charge of the Ministries of Rites and War while concurrently serving as banner general.

sentences.zh: 尋拜文淵閣大學士，命赴山東查辦鹽務，校閱浙江營伍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Deepness, ordered to go to Shandong to investigate salt affairs, and to inspect Zhejiang military units.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Deepness, ordered to Shandong to investigate salt affairs, and assigned to inspect Zhejiang military units.

sentences.zh: 三十年，文宗即位，應詔陳言，略曰：「求治莫先於用人、理財、行政諸大端。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, responding to an edict he stated his views, saying in summary: 'Seeking good governance must begin with the great matters of employing men, managing finances, and administering affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, when Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, he responded to an edict with his views, writing in summary: 'Good governance must begin with the great tasks of employing men, managing finances, and running the administration.

sentences.zh: 用人之道，明試以功。

translations.literal: The way to employ men is to test them clearly by achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The way to employ men is to test them clearly by their achievements.

sentences.zh: 人有剛柔，才有長短。

translations.literal: Men have hardness and softness; talent has strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: Men differ in temperament, and talents differ in strength.

sentences.zh: 用違其才，君子亦恐誤事；

translations.literal: Use a man against his talent, and even a gentleman may fail in the task;
translations.idiomatic: Use a man against his talents, and even an upright man may fail;

sentences.zh: 用得其當，小人亦能濟事。

translations.literal: use him fittingly, and even a petty man can accomplish the work.
translations.idiomatic: use him fittingly, and even a lesser man can get the job done.

sentences.zh: 設官分職，非為眾人藏身之地。

translations.literal: Establishing offices and dividing duties is not to provide hiding places for the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Offices and duties exist not to give everyone a place to hide.

sentences.zh: 實心任事者，雖小人當保全；

translations.literal: Those who earnestly take on affairs, even if petty men, should be preserved;
translations.idiomatic: Those who earnestly take on their duties, even if they are lesser men, should be kept;

sentences.zh: 不肯任怨者，雖君子當委置。

translations.literal: those unwilling to bear responsibility, even if gentlemen, should be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: those unwilling to bear responsibility, even if they are gentlemen, should be set aside.

sentences.zh: 行政在於得人，迂腐之說，無裨時務，泥古之論，難合機宜，財非人不理。

translations.literal: Administering affairs lies in obtaining the right men; pedantic talk does not help current business, antiquarian argument does not suit present needs, and finances cannot be managed without the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Good administration depends on finding the right men. Pedantic talk does not help present needs, antiquarian argument does not suit the times, and finances cannot be managed without capable people.

sentences.zh: 今賦額四千餘萬，支用有餘，不能如額，以致短絀。

translations.literal: Now the tax quota is more than forty million, enough for expenditures with surplus, yet collection cannot meet the quota, causing shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: The tax quota is more than forty million taels—enough to cover expenditures with a surplus—yet collection falls short and creates deficits.

sentences.zh: 致絀之由，非探本窮源，不能通盤清釐。

translations.literal: The causes of shortfall cannot be cleared comprehensively without tracing to the root and probing the source.
translations.idiomatic: The causes of deficit cannot be cleared up comprehensively without tracing them to the root.

sentences.zh: 與其正賦外別費經營，不如於正賦中覈實籌畫。

translations.literal: Rather than raising funds separately outside regular taxes, it is better to plan realistically within regular taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Rather than raising extra funds outside regular taxes, it is better to plan realistically within the regular tax system.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，特諭曰：「身為端揆，一言一動，舉朝所矜式。

translations.literal: ' When the memorial entered, a special edict said: 'As chief minister, every word and act is a model for the whole court.
translations.idiomatic: ' When the memorial reached the throne, a special edict declared: 'As chief minister, your every word and act is a model for the whole court.

sentences.zh: 耆英率意敷陳，持論過偏，顯違古訓，流弊曷可勝言。

translations.literal: Qiying stated his views at will; his argument was too one-sided, clearly violated ancient teaching, and the resulting evils cannot all be told.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying stated his views too freely. His argument was one-sided, clearly violated ancient teaching, and the harm it could do is beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 」傳旨申飭。

translations.literal: ' An imperial message rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: ' An imperial message rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 耆英不自安，屢稱病。

translations.literal: Qiying was ill at ease and repeatedly claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying grew uneasy and repeatedly pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 是年十月，上手詔揭示穆彰阿及耆英罪狀，斥「耆英在廣東抑民奉夷，謾許入城，幾致不測之變。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year the emperor personally issued an edict revealing the offenses of Mujangga and Qiying, condemning 'Qiying in Guangdong for suppressing the people and serving the barbarians, falsely promising entry into the city, nearly causing unforeseen disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year the emperor personally issued an edict listing the offenses of Mujangga and Qiying, condemning 'Qiying in Guangdong for suppressing the people to please the foreigners, falsely promising them entry into the city, and nearly causing disaster.

sentences.zh: 數面陳夷情可畏，應事周旋，但圖常保祿位。

translations.literal: Repeatedly stating in audience that barbarian conditions were to be feared, dealing with affairs by compromise, seeking only to preserve rank and salary.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly told the throne in audience that the foreigners were to be feared, handled affairs by compromise, and sought only to keep his rank and salary.

sentences.zh: 穆彰阿暗而難明，耆英顯而易見，貽害國家，其罪則一」。

translations.literal: Mujangga was hidden and hard to discern, Qiying was obvious and easy to see; both harmed the state, and their crime was one.'
translations.idiomatic: Mujangga worked in the shadows and was hard to pin down; Qiying acted openly for all to see. Both harmed the state, and their crime was the same.'

sentences.zh: 猶念其迫於時勢，從寬降為部屬。

translations.literal: Still mindful that he had been forced by circumstances of the time, leniency was shown and he was demoted to a subordinate post.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that he had been constrained by the circumstances of his time, the court showed leniency and demoted him to a subordinate post.

sentences.zh: 尋補工部員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was given a supplementary appointment as assistant director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given a supplementary appointment as assistant director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪北犯，耆英子馬蘭鎮總兵慶錫奏請父子兄弟同赴軍前，命耆英隨巡防王大臣效力，以捐餉予四品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng the southern rebels invaded northward; Qiying's son Qingxi, brigade general of Malan, memorialized requesting that father, sons, and brothers go together to the front; Qiying was ordered to serve with the frontier defense princes and grandees, and for donating military funds was given fourth-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 the southern rebels marched north. Qiying's son Qingxi, brigade general of Malan, memorialized asking that father, sons, and brothers serve together at the front. Qiying was ordered to serve with the frontier defense princes and grandees and was given fourth-rank insignia for contributing military funds.

sentences.zh: 五年，慶錫向屬員借貸被劾，耆英坐私告，革職圈禁。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Qingxi was impeached for borrowing from subordinates; Qiying was punished for private denunciation, stripped of office, and placed under house arrest.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Qingxi was impeached for borrowing money from his subordinates. Qiying was punished for making a private report, stripped of office, and placed under house arrest.

sentences.zh: 八年，英人糾合法、美、俄諸國兵船犯天津，爭改條約，命大學士桂良、尚書花沙納扆往查辦。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the English gathered French, American, and Russian warships to attack Tianjin and demand revision of the treaty; Grand Secretary Guiliang and Minister Huashana were ordered to proceed and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Britain assembled French, American, and Russian warships to attack Tianjin and demand treaty revisions. Grand Secretary Guiliang and Minister Huashana were ordered to go and investigate.

sentences.zh: 巡防王大臣薦耆英熟悉情形，召對，自陳原力任其難，予侍郎銜，赴天津協議。

translations.literal: The frontier defense princes and grandees recommended Qiying as familiar with conditions; he was summoned for audience, stated that he had originally been willing to bear the difficulty, was given vice minister rank, and sent to Tianjin to negotiate.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier defense princes and grandees recommended Qiying as familiar with the situation. Summoned for audience, he said he had always been willing to take on the hard task. He was given vice minister rank and sent to Tianjin to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 初耆英之在廣東也，五口通商事多由裁決，一意遷就。

translations.literal: When Qiying had been in Guangdong, matters of trade at the five ports were largely decided by his rulings, and he yielded on every point.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiying had been in Guangdong, trade affairs at the five treaty ports had largely been decided by his rulings, and he had yielded on every point.

sentences.zh: 七年冬，廣州陷，檔案為英人所得，譯出耆英章奏，多掩飾不實，深惡之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year Guangzhou fell; archives were taken by the English, and Qiying's memorials were translated—many concealed the truth and were deeply hated by them.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventh year Guangzhou fell. The British seized the archives and translated Qiying's memorials, many of which concealed the truth. They came to despise him deeply.

sentences.zh: 及至天津，英人拒不見，惶恐求去，不候旨，回通州，於是欺謾之跡益彰，為王大臣論劾，嚴詔逮治，賜自盡。

translations.literal: When he reached Tianjin the English refused to see him; in fear he begged to leave, returned to Tongzhou without awaiting orders, and thus the signs of deception became still clearer; impeached by the princes and grandees, a stern edict ordered his arrest and granted him suicide.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Tianjin the British refused to see him. In fear he begged to leave and returned to Tongzhou without waiting for orders. His deceit now stood exposed. The princes and grandees impeached him, a stern edict ordered his arrest, and he was granted suicide.

sentences.zh: 論曰：罷戰言和，始發於琦善，去備媚敵，致敗之由。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Ending the war and speaking of peace began with Qi Shan; abandoning preparedness and courting the enemy was the cause of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: The decision to stop fighting and sue for peace began with Qi Shan. Abandoning preparedness and courting the enemy was what led to defeat.

sentences.zh: 伊里布有忍辱負重之心，無安危定傾之略，且廟謨未定，廷議紛紜，至江寧城下之盟，乃與耆英結束和議，損威喪權，貽害莫挽。

translations.literal: Yi Libu had the heart to endure humiliation and bear heavy burdens but lacked a strategy to secure safety and stabilize crisis; moreover court policy was unsettled and court debate was divided; when the alliance was made below the walls of Jiangning, he and Qiying concluded the peace, losing prestige and surrendering authority, with harm that could not be retrieved.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Libu was willing to endure humiliation and bear heavy burdens, but he lacked a strategy to save the dynasty in crisis. Court policy was unsettled and debate was divided. When the treaty was signed below the walls of Jiangning, he and Qiying closed the peace negotiations, surrendering prestige and authority in a loss that could never be undone.

sentences.zh: 耆英獨任善後，留廣州入城之隙，兵釁再開，浸致庚申之禍。

translations.literal: Qiying alone bore postwar arrangements, left the opening for entry into Guangzhou city, hostilities reopened, and gradually led to the disaster of Gengshen.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying alone handled the postwar arrangements and left open the question of foreign entry into Guangzhou. Fighting broke out again and eventually led to the Gengshen disaster.

sentences.zh: 三人者同受惡名，而耆英不保其身命，宜哉。

translations.literal: All three alike bore evil reputations, yet Qiying alone could not preserve his life—as was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: All three earned the same ill repute, yet Qiying alone could not save his life—and that was only fitting.
